case_name: Laxmibai Nagappa Matiwadar And Ors. vs Limbabai Nagappa Matiwadar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Laxmibai Nagappa Matiwadar and others (wife, husband's relatives)

facts_of_case: Suit filed by respondent for possession of three plots relying on her right to succeed to the interest of her husband Nagappa. Appellants' marriage was void, and children born from this marriage were illegitimate.

legal_principles.principle: Legitimacy under section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act confers status on children born out of void and voidable marriages.
legal_principles.held: The Joint Committee's report clearly indicates that in no case, the off-springs of void or voidable marriage be regarded as illegitimate.

legal_principles.principle: The express declaration in section 16(1) of the Act takes away and eclipses the general rule that the off-spring of a marriage, which is null and void ipso jure, is illegitimate.
legal_principles.held: Though because of the statue the marriage would be void, that would not lead to the inevitable result of bastardising the children who are born out of such a void wedlock.

legal_principles.principle: The legitimacy conferred by section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act recognises rights in or to the property of parents.
legal_principles.held: Section 16 thus enacts a complete Code with regard to the off-springs of void or voidable marriages. Firstly, it declares the status of such a child being one as legitimate. Secondly, it recognises rights in the property of the parents.

outcome.final_order: Suit decreed with regard to Plot No. 228, holding that appellants would not have any right or interest therein because appellant No. 1 Laxmibai's marriage was void.

keywords: Bombay Prevention of Hindu Bigamous Act
Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
